datasetInformation.datasetDescription: These data were acquired by the Geological Survey of Canada (GSC) in collaboration with the U.S. Geological Survey (USGS).  Data were acquired over a five-year period (2007 to 2011) in the high Arctic Ocean with the Canadian Coast Guard Icebreaker Louis S. St-Laurent.  In the four-year period 2008 to 2011, the St-Laurent was accompanied by the US Coast Guard Icebreaker Healy.
datasetInformation.purpose: These data were acquired principally for the purposes of establishing the outer limits of the extended continental shelf for the United States and Canada in the Arctic Ocean under the provisions of the Convention on the Law of the Sea.

processingParameters.processingStep:
PROCESSING (John Shimeld, February 2013)                                    
1:  read SEG-D; navigation; delays; rcvr statics; design CMP bins @ 12.5m.  
2:  FK filt; bandpass w/source ghost notch & extreme noise lowcut; debias.  
3:  common rcvr sort; trc edit; noise model & subtract; depspike; FX decon. 
4:  surface related multiple model on shot gathers (Verschuur et al. 1992). 
5:  minimum phase conversion using measured wavelets from each source array.
6:  adaptive subtraction of multiple model (Wang 2003).                     
7:  surface consistent gapped decon (48/250ms gap/filtlen; 2 design gates); 
     CMP sort; NMO correction (30% stretch mute); residual statics.          
8:  diversity stack w/sqrt normalisation.                                   
9:  zero phase conversion; despike; FX decon (120 ms/trc; 19 trc mix);      
     runmix (3 trc; weights: 0.2/0.6/0.2); time-varying bandpass filter      
     (0-1s 2/5/80/120Hz; 1.5-2.5s 4/6/40/65Hz; 3-12s 5.5/7/35/50Hz).         
10: finite difference migration w/sedimentary velocity func. from sonobuoys;
     FK filt wrap-around multiples (0701e,0701f,0702b,0702c,0702f,0930,1010).
11: time-varying bandpass (as above); balance (1s gates with 50% overlap).  
     add CMP navigation; resample (4 ms); SEG-Y (byte17:SP; byte21:CMP;      
     byte81: latitude in arcsec*100; byte85:longitude in arcsec*100).
